rule_en: Year-count ('transmission'): divide the current year of life by 12 and count the remainder from a starting point, counting the starting sign as 1. Worked example: 35th year, remainder 11, counted from Virgo (Ascendant and Mars), reaches Cancer (Saturn). This equals one sign per year: sign = start + (completed years mod 12).
locator: Valens IV.11 'The Operative Year and the Method of Fractions'; Riley tr. printed p.78 (PDF p.80); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.174, Pingree p.164
notes: Inclusive counting is confirmed by the example (Virgo=1 … Cancer=11). Valens frames it as one star 'transmitting' the year to another, not as a single 'lord of the year'.

rule_en: Count the years from the Sun, the Moon and the Ascendant. If the count ends in an empty sign, the year is handed to that sign's ruler. Also count from Fortune, Daimon, Love and Necessity. Counting from the angles is 'more scientific'.

rule_en: Judging general fortune from the triplicity lords. (1) Take the sect light: Sun by day, Moon by night. (2) Find its triangle (sign triplicity) and that triangle's predominant houseruler (first lord for the sect) and its helper (second lord). (3) Grade each lord by position. At an angle (ASC, MC or another operative sign) = fortunate and illustrious. Following an angle = moderate. Preceding an angle = base and unfortunate. Also note rising/setting, own signs, and benefic or malefic aspects. (4) Check the light itself and its aspects.
locator: Valens II.2 'The Distinguishing Characteristics of the Triangles, the Houserulers, the Helpers, and the Sects of the Sun and the Moon'; Riley tr. printed p.25 (PDF p.27); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.56, Pingree p.55
notes: The order of the lords per sect is in II.1 (valens.triplicity.*). PDF p.28 spells it out per triangle for a Sun in each element by day, e.g. Sun in an earth sign: look at Venus, then the Moon, then Mars. For night births use the Moon 'in the same manner'.
quote_withheld: Riley translation in copyright: see the locator

rule_en: Time split between the first two triplicity lords. First lord badly placed but the next well placed (angular): ups and downs in the early years, then vigour and effectiveness (though still unsteady and anxious). First lord well placed but the next badly placed: success first, then a fall. The switch comes 'at the rising time of the sign' or 'the cyclical return of the chronocrator'; for a fall, from the rising time of the sign where the succeeding lord is badly placed. Both well placed: lasting, remarkable fortune.
locator: Valens II.2; Riley tr. printed p.25 (PDF p.27); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.57, Pingree p.56
notes: Valens gives early-life vs later-life roles only for the first ('predominant'/'preceding') and second ('successor'/'succeeding') lords. Unlike later authors, he does NOT give the third (co-working) lord its own period in this chapter, nor divide life into thirds. 'Rising time of the sign' refers to the ascensional-times system of later books; he promises to clarify the chronocrator 'at the appropriate time'. II.21K;22P worked examples (PDF p.38-39) show 'first years humble' when the first lord precedes an angle, with later rise when the partner is angular.

data.switch_point: rising time of the sign / cyclical return of the chronocrator (not a fixed age)

rule_en: Lot of Fortune as a second Ascendant. Find whether the Lot is angular, succedent or cadent, and find its ruler. Ruler in the Ascendant by day, or another operative place, with the Sun, Moon or benefics in aspect = noble, distinguished, fortunate. At other angles or succedent = moderate. Preceding an angle = crises and ruin. Derived places: the Lot = Life; 10th from it = Rank (MC); 7th = Descendant; 4th = IC; the rest as the twelve places.
locator: Valens II.17K;18P 'The Lot of Fortune as the Ascendant'; Riley tr. printed p.34 (PDF p.36); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.79, Pingree p.76
notes: Same chapter: 'Likewise look for the ruler of the Lot. If it is in the Ascendant during the day or is in some other operative place, with the sun, the moon, or benefics in aspect, it will make the native noble, distinguished, and fortunate.'

topic: ruler of the Lot of Fortune
rule_en: The Lot of Fortune and its ruler judge livelihood and rank when the triplicity lords fail (II.2). The Lot concerns the body and the work of one's hands (II.19). Its 11th place (Accomplishment) gives property (II.20). In II.3 Fortune is 'the most influential and most potent place'; examine its ruler and the stars at or square/trine to it.
locator: Valens II.3 'The Lot of Fortune and its Houseruler'; Riley tr. printed p.26 (PDF p.28); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.59, Pingree p.58
notes: Valens never uses a modern phrase like 'ruler of Fortune = livelihood'. The livelihood link rests on II.2 (Lot and ruler examined for prosperity), II.19K;20P (Fortune = body and work of hands, PDF p.37) and II.20K;21P (Accomplishment = property, PDF p.37). See also valens.lot.fortune.meaning and valens.lot.accomplishment.

topic: ruler of the Lot of Fortune
rule_en: Best when the ruler of Daimon is at the Lot of Fortune or at its 10th place (i.e. at its MC) = illustrious. Ruler turned away, cadent, or with malefics = exile and distress abroad.
locator: Valens II.19K;20P 'The Lot of Fortune and Daimon'; Riley tr. printed p.35 (PDF p.37); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.81, Pingree p.78

topic: ruler of the Lot of Fortune
rule_en: For injury and disease, the sign of the Lot of Fortune and especially the sign its ruler occupies indicate the affected part. Daimon and its ruler clarify it. A Book IV worked example (PDF p.77) reads injury from the sign the Lot's ruler occupies (ruler in Cancer = breast and stomach).
locator: Valens II.36K;37P 'Injuries and Diseases, with Examples'; Riley tr. printed p.49 (PDF p.51); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.111, Pingree p.106
notes: Chapter heading is on PDF p.49; the quoted rule is on PDF p.51.
